upsc.label: Parliamentary system — defining institutional feature / executive responsibility

uppcs.label: Rule of Law / access to justice

political-theory.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** executive responsibility; limited government; State restraint; liberty under law; equality as absence of privilege; rights–duties correlation; Rule of Law; separation of powers; natural justice.
- **Recurring traps:** parliamentary ≠ mere election; Constitution ≠ constitutionalism; liberty ≠ unrestricted action; equality ≠ identical treatment in all circumstances; due process ≠ textual phrase “procedure established by law”; State ≠ nation.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *best definition*, *most appropriate*, *chief purpose*, *main advantage*, *by definition*, *implied institutionally*.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC heavily conceptual/best-fit/elimination; UPPCS comparatively direct on origin/core feature and uses Assertion–Reason.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2023 directly revisited due process + purpose of Constitution; UPPCS 2025 revisited parliamentary responsibility + Rule of Law.

parts-schedules.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Schedule-subject association; Part-subject association; Article-institution/provision association; three legislative Lists; language additions; anti-defection exceptions; Ninth Schedule immunity limits.
- **Recurring traps:** `within 6 months` vs `after 6 months`; Speaker/Chairman vs President/Governor; 1/3 split vs 2/3 merger; judicial protection vs blanket immunity; “official language” vs Eighth Schedule language vs classical language.
- **Qualifier patterns:** `NOT correctly matched`, `only`, `within/after`, `which Part/Schedule`, exact Article number, List classification.
- **UPSC:** conceptual fine print + statement elimination + judicial doctrine.
- **UPPCS:** wider rote mapping density; near-identical Article/Schedule pairs.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2024–25 → Parts, Eighth/Seventh Schedule, anti-defection; UPPCS 2024–25 → Articles, Lists, Parts and Schedules.

upsc.label: Initiation / bicameral passage / joint sitting / assent

amendments-basic-structure.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Art. 368 procedure; special majority; State ratification; Basic Structure; judicial review; amendment-case chronology.
- **Recurring traps:** `either House ≠ Lok Sabha only`; `≥½ States ≠ all States`; `no prior recommendation ≠ no presidential assent`; `no joint sitting`; `special majority ≠ ⅔ of total membership`.
- **Qualifier pattern:** “only”, “all States”, “prior recommendation”, “shall give assent”, “not less than one-half”.
- **UPSC:** statement-heavy; exact constitutional wording + judicial doctrine; increasingly tests whether a *specific provision* requires State ratification.
- **UPPCS:** greater direct recall of amendment number/year, case names and chronological ordering.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2024–25 and UPPCS 2024–25 again tested Article 368 mechanics/ratification rather than generic amendment theory.

upsc.label: Preamble as expression of framers’ intent

preamble.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** exact Preamble vocabulary; objectives; part/enforceability distinction; original vs amended formulation.
- **Recurring traps:** current wording substituted for 1950 wording; `part of Constitution` ≠ `independently enforceable`; non-Preamble words inserted as distractors.
- **Qualifier patterns:** **NOT**, **exact**, **legal nature**, **in that order**, **inserted by 42nd Amendment**.
- **UPSC:** conceptual/legal distinctions + historical constitutional status.
- **UPPCS:** higher literal-recall load—word counts, amendment words, presence/absence; taxonomy additionally requires source-country mapping.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPPCS 2025 again tested 42nd-Amendment insertion.

upsc.label: Single citizenship + domicile; naturalised citizen; deprivation

uppcs.label: Article 2 vs Article 3; authority to create/rename States

union-states-citizenship.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Part II/Arts. 5–11; single citizenship; acquisition/loss; Parliament’s power; Arts. 2–4; chronology of State formation.
- **Recurring traps:** citizen by birth ≠ only person eligible for President; citizenship can be deprived in statutorily specified cases; Article 2 ≠ Article 3; State legislature gives **views**, not consent.
- **Qualifier patterns:** “only”; “not correctly matched”; “under Article 3”; “earliest to latest”; “came into existence on basis of…”.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → conceptual/legal-basis pair/statement traps; UPPCS → direct provision recall + chronology.
- **Recent reinforcement:** State formation/legal basis in UPSC 2025; State-power matching in UPPCS 2024; chronology in UPPCS 2025.

upsc.label: Article 13: law / ordinance / abridgment of FR

fundamental-rights.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Article 21 expansion; article↔right mapping; writ applicability; Article 14 equality/non-arbitrariness; citizen vs person; property after 44th Amendment.
- **Recurring traps:** Art 17 ≠ Right against Exploitation; property ≠ Art 19; Art 29(1) ≠ minority-only; prohibition ≠ certiorari; Art 32 ≠ Art 226; preventive detention ≠ ordinary arrest safeguards.
- **Qualifier patterns:** `only`, `not`, `any person`, `citizen`, `public duty`, `lower court`, `how many`, assertion–reason, exact article/amendment.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC increasingly tests doctrine/application and statement elimination; UPPCS more often tests direct article/amendment/writ recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2024 privacy + prohibition; 2025 ordinance/Art 24; **2026 Article 13 definition of law**. UPPCS 2024 reinforced Article 19, equality availability and exploitation.

upsc.label: Fundamental Duties — list / nature / negative identification
PESA — Gram Sabha powers / statutory qualifiers
Fifth/Sixth Schedule — purpose / land protection / consequences / administration

uppcs.label: Part mapping — Scheduled & Tribal Areas = Part X

scheduled-tribal-areas.synthesis:
- recurring concepts: Fifth vs Sixth; tribal-land protection; Scheduled Area declaration; State/Governor/Union roles; PESA Gram Sabha; ST notification; PVTG criteria.
- recurring traps:
  - President declares Scheduled Area ≠ Governor.
  - Governor reports to **President** ≠ CM reports to Home Ministry.
  - Fifth Schedule ≠ automatic autonomous local government.
  - Scheduled Area declaration ≠ State executive power ceases.
  - PESA mining recommendation = **minor minerals**, not any mineral.
  - PESA ≠ creation of autonomous tribal regions.
  - ST status = State/UT-specific.
- qualifier patterns: **minor**, **not more than**, **as nearly as may be**, **annually or whenever required**, **consulted** vs **recommendation mandatory**.
- UPSC vs UPPCS: UPSC → statement/consequence/qualifier elimination; UPPCS → direct Schedule–State–Part–year recall.
- recent reinforcement: continuous UPSC testing from 2022–2026 on Scheduled Area consequences, notification, ST recognition and Fifth/Sixth distinction.

rights-legislation.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** custody status; State control of prisons/parole; statutory-right architecture; teacher-qualification authority; disability-accessibility framework; consumer complaint rights; cyber-reporting duty.
- **Recurring traps:** `right ≠ concession`; `Code ≠ Act`; `Central framework ≠ State administration`; correct institution/Ministry; correct enactment year; exact statutory qualifier.
- **Qualifier patterns:** “legally mandatory”, “all/only”, “standard size”, “right”, “minimum qualification”, “under which Act”.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → multi-statement legal precision + Act/action pairing; UPPCS → amendment/year/scheme association + direct legal-rule recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** 2023 sharply reinforced prisons + Flag Code + Act/offence matching; 2026 returned to disability law with a three-part statute/scheme/institution trap.

upsc.label: Presiding officers / removal / Deputy Speaker rules
Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha / special Rajya Sabha powers

parliament.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** presiding officers > budget/financial control > committees > Money/Financial Bills > lapse/joint sitting > House asymmetry > devices/sessions.
- **Recurring traps:** `may ≠ shall`; `recommend ≠ amend`; effective majority ≠ absolute majority; `2/3 present & voting ≠ 2/3 total membership`; President is part of Parliament but not either House; Chairman of RS ≠ member, Deputy Chairman = member.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *only*, *not*, *final*, *present and voting*, *all the then members*, *within 14 days*, *more than six months*, *first session*.
- **UPSC:** increasingly procedural/qualifier-heavy; 2022–26 reinforces Deputy Speaker, Ethics Committee, Speaker removal, lapse, Question Hour and committee composition.
- **UPPCS:** more direct Article-number, seat-number, committee-size, state-representation and office-holder chronology recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2024–26 + UPPCS 2025 strongly reinforce presiding officers, joint sitting, committees and precise majority formulae.

uppcs.label: PIL / judicial review / access to justice

judiciary.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Art. 131 original jurisdiction; Art. 142; guardian/custodian role; appointment/removal safeguards; judicial review; NALSA/legal-aid eligibility; Gram Nyayalayas; contempt; constitutional location of tribunals.
- **Recurring traps:** original ≠ appellate; exclusive original Art.131 ≠ exclusive power to test Central laws; judicial review ≠ review petition; constitutional removal majority ≠ statutory inquiry procedure; ordinary Lok Adalat ≠ Permanent Lok Adalat.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *exclusive*, *only*, *cannot*, *all*, *constitutional vs statutory*, *may vs shall*, *pending vs pre-litigation*, *civil only vs civil + criminal*.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC repeatedly tests legal effect/qualifiers and Constitution–statute boundaries; UPPCS more often tests Article/Part mapping, personalities, one-step institutional facts and current/history hooks.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC—Contempt (2022); UPPCS—tribunal + judge resignation (2023), PIL/access-to-justice (2025).

union-executive.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** nominal vs real executive; CoM responsibility; presidential electoral college/vote value; President–VP contrasts; Cabinet Secretariat; AG status/rights.
- **Recurring traps:** `Parliament` ≠ `Lok Sabha`; President ≠ PM as repository of Union executive power; President ≠ MP though part of Parliament; nominated MPs: President election ✗, VP election ✓; Cabinet Secretary ≠ PM; Cabinet Secretariat ≠ PMO.
- **Qualifier patterns:** “elected”, “nominated”, “both Houses”, “House of the People”, “total membership”, “may reconsider once”, “not entitled to vote”, “limited judicial review”.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → constitutional fine print + elimination; UPPCS → Article/post mapping, VP, PMO and chronology.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2025 directly reinforced **ordinance limits + pardoning power**; UPPCS 2025 reinforced **VP status + Presidential chronology**.

state-executive-legislature.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Governor’s constitutional position; discretion; tenure/removal; immunity; dual charge; Legislative Council size/permanence; Speaker continuity; Chief Secretary; provision mapping.
- **Recurring traps:** “Governor for each State” ≠ different person for every State; 5-year term ≠ security for full 5 years; no constitutional removal procedure ≠ arbitrary/unreviewable removal; Council ≠ Rajya Sabha in powers; permanent ≠ cannot be abolished.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *same person, not, cannot, during term, first session, fixed tenure, not more than, at least, one-third, two-thirds*.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → statement-combination, institutional nuance, immunity/discretion/commission traps. UPPCS → Article-number/heading + numerical recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2025 revisited Governor discretion and Article 361 immunity; UPPCS 2024 revisited Articles 153–156 and dual charge.

upsc.label: Parliament legislating on State subjects / legislative relations

federalism-emergency.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** Art. 249; Art. 253; federal vs unitary/centralising traits; Art. 356 consequences; State–Centre division over minor minerals.
- **Recurring traps:** “State consent required”; “special majority” without specifying formula; automatic Assembly dissolution; Art. 19 suspension under President’s Rule; States’ right to secede; Centre alone makes minor-mineral concession rules.
- **Qualifier patterns:** `necessarily`, `exclusive`, `national interest`, `present and voting`, `constitutional`, `can/may` vs `automatically`.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → functional/procedural elimination; UPPCS → article/commission/thinker matching + direct constitutional characterization.
- **Recent reinforcement:** minor-mineral competence repeated 2019 → 2025; constitutional status of Inter-State Council tested in 2025.

uppcs.label: Gram Sabha / composition / reservation / age / tenure

local-government.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** constitutionalisation; democratic decentralisation; Gram Sabha; 3-tier structure; SEC/SFC; reservation; 5-year duration; local planning.
- **Recurring traps:** 73rd ≠ 74th; DPC belongs Part IX-A/74th; SEC ≠ ECI; Governor ≠ CM for SFC; minimum age 21 ≠ 25/30; Gram Sabha = registered electors ≠ all residents; intermediate tier has ≤20-lakh exception.
- **Qualifier patterns:** “not correct”; “all States”; “minimum”; “not less than”; “sole responsibility”; “who constitutes”; “only”.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → statement elimination + conceptual decentralisation; UPPCS → direct Part/Article/date/committee/authority recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2025–26 → intermediate tier/SFC + reservation; UPPCS 2024–25 → amendment mapping, SEC, Part IX-A, age, women reservation, tenure.

elections.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** elector qualification; candidate qualification/disqualification; plurality vs majority; delimitation authority/finality/count; legislative reservation; voting-age amendment.
- **Recurring traps:** “resident of constituency” ≠ “elector”; “largest votes” ≠ “absolute majority”; disqualification ≠ permanent; laid before House ≠ alterable by House; reserved seat ≠ separate electorate.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *only*, *at least*, *permanently*, *cannot be challenged*, *cannot modify*, *how many*, chronology.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → legal/constitutional qualifiers + statement elimination; UPPCS → direct amendment/year/party/reform chronology recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** delimitation count (UPSC 2024); election-reform chronology (UPPCS 2025). No forecast beyond observed patterns.

governance-regulators.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** legal status; enabling Act; parent ministry/department; exact statutory mandate; certification-mark owner; identity vs citizenship; e-governance platform purpose.
- **Recurring traps:** institution created **under an Act** vs executive/society; administering ministry ≠ statute; similarly named directorates; regulator’s sector ≠ every activity in that sector.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *statutory*, *first*, *directly*, *mandatory*, *under*, *nodal*, *proof of*, *only*, *how many*.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC increasingly combines 2–3 attributes per row; UPPCS adds direct factual recall of newly launched portals, reports and sponsoring ministries.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2025 uses organization–function–ministry row matching; UPPCS 2025 uses current portal/report/ministry attribution.
- **No unsupported forecasting:** plausible variants limited to the same transformations—body ↔ Act; body ↔ ministry; body ↔ function; mark ↔ authority; digital platform ↔ purpose.

upsc.label: B. Planning architecture: Planning Commission → NITI; NDC

uppcs.label: A. NITI / Planning Commission status + legacy

statutory-bodies.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** institutional source/status; planning architecture; composition; appointment/selection; constitutional provision ↔ statutory Act mapping.
- **Recurring traps:** non-constitutional ≠ non-statutory; NDC ≠ Planning Commission organ; ISC ≠ Zonal Council; Lokpal ≠ constitutional body; “Chairperson can be CJI” ≠ “only CJI can be Chairperson.”
- **Qualifier patterns:** `how many`, `only`, `not`, `established as per Constitution`, `maximum`, `not less than`, `in/outside India`.
- **UPSC vs UPPCS:** UPSC → multi-body classification + qualifier-heavy statutory statements; UPPCS → direct institution-person/source/committee recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2023 + two 2025 institutional-status/Lokpal questions; UPPCS 2024 Lokpal selection.

constitutional-bodies.synthesis:
- **Recurring concepts:** constitutional article ↔ body; appointing/removing authority; reports; function boundaries; FC devolution formula; CAG–PAC chain.
- **Recurring traps:** `recommend ≠ decide`; `appointment authority ≠ removal authority`; `constitutional body ≠ statutory/executive body`; exact article-number matching.
- **Qualifier patterns:** *only*, *not*, *correctly/not correctly matched*, *how many*, multi-statement combinations.
- **UPSC:** narrower bodies, but deeper qualifier-heavy testing—especially FC criteria/recommendations and ECI/CAG functional limits.
- **UPPCS:** broader body coverage + direct article/composition/chairperson/appointment-removal recall.
- **Recent reinforcement:** UPSC 2023 + 2025 → 15th FC; UPPCS 2023–25 → article mapping, ECI/UPSC functions, FC chairpersons.
- **Direct recurring-PYQ variants worth covering:** FC criteria across successive commissions; CEC vs EC removal; UPSC vs SPSC appointment/removal; Art. 338/338A/338B/340 differentiation.
